- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates prices; adjust downward bias or increase volatility buffer.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast growth by 10–20% for next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after rising, or reverses from high to low), model often fails to recognize it; add a “reversion penalty” to forecast: if recent 5-day avg is > 10% above 30d avg, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trends; if sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2) for 5+ days, reduce forecast slope to avoid “trend trap”.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from history (e.g., >15% from 30d moving avg), model often ignores it; apply “sentiment-triggered correction”: if sentiment > 0.5 for 3 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with market sentiment.
